location: sections/limits.tex 455-458 and 481-487 (Prop lim:prop:setgrowth); summary sentences at limits.tex 20-21 and intro.tex 133
issue: The statement says every corrected-grid certificate of accuracy eps, including its filtering history, has a last-stage grid with at least 1+1/(2 sqrt eps) nodes per coordinate. The proof uses only the filtering rule with threshold U >= OPT = 0, which never removes an interval. A valid path certificate (Def def:cert) may remove any interval whose endpoint min-marginals are >= beta, and here beta < 0. Exact counterexample: n=2, F=(x1-x2)^2, eps=1/50. Stage 0 is the uniform grid of step 1/5 on [0,1]^2, where all min-marginals are -1/50. Stage 1 is the box [0,1/5]^2 with grid {0,1/5}^2, where min Q = -1/50. With beta=-1/50 and xhat=0, (C1) and (C2) hold and the gap is eps, yet the last grid has 2 nodes instead of the claimed >= 4.54. Script: process/w2/checks/r4_setgrowth_cert.py, which also covers n=3 and n=4.
fix: Replace 'Hence every corrected-grid certificate of accuracy eps, including its filtering history, has a last-stage grid ...' with: 'Hence every run of the filtering method with thresholds U_j >= OPT (in particular every run of Algorithms 1 and 2) that certifies accuracy eps ends with a grid of at least 1+1/(2 sqrt eps) nodes in every coordinate. A general path certificate may remove intervals whose min-marginals lie in [beta,0], so its last grid can be small, but its stage-0 grid then has gaps of length at most 2 sqrt eps on the removed part.' At limits.tex 20-21 and intro.tex 133, say 'does not bound the grids produced by filtering'.

issue: The proof shows that the run with constant answers gp makes at least |C|-1 evaluations. That run is not a run on any admissible F_c, while the statement claims the bound 'on some F_c'. In the randomized part, 'the run on the constant answers has at most Q evaluations' is not justified.
fix: Add: 'For c in C let t_c be the index of the first evaluation of the constant run that lies in B(c,r). The run on F_c agrees with the constant run up to and including evaluation t_c. Only the c whose ball contains y can lack such an index. Since each point lies in at most one ball, the finite t_c are distinct, so some F_c forces at least |C|-1 evaluations.' In the randomized part, write 'consider the first Q evaluations of the run on the constant answers'.
